subject: Clarify: multi-regional subprocessor ownership, on-call mapping & crypto custody for EU payment paths
messages:
From: Lucia Marquez <lucia.marquez@helixbank.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@helixbank.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request for subprocessor residency + key custody mapping for EU payment flows

Naomi,

Thanks for taking this — Helix Bank is in the middle of a SIG/SOC2 deep-dive for our payments integration. We need a concise mapping focused on the EU payment path: which Redwood subprocessors handle tokenization, K/V cache, ephemeral keys, or any telemetry that could touch payment metadata. For each subprocessor please provide:

- Primary hosting region(s) and data residency (e.g., eu-west-1)
- Whether they hold persistent keys or only ephemeral material (if keys: HSM/KMS provider + FIPS attestations if available)
- On-call escalation contact (name + role) and primary SLA for incident response
- Any subcontracting (i.e., does that subprocessor rely on additional subprocessors)

We have a one-week timeline for evidence. Attached is our Helix_Subproc_Template.xlsx — feel free to populate a CSV if easier. Also flag any items that would require an NDA or redaction.

Appreciate a point estimate for delivery.

Best,
Lucia
Lucia Marquez
Senior Third-Party Risk Analyst — Helix Bank
Helix Compliance

Attachment: Helix_Subproc_Template.xlsx (template, see request)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 10:01:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: Request for subprocessor residency + key custody mapping for EU payment flows

Forwarding Helix's ask. TL;DR: they want an EU-focused mapping for payment-related paths and explicit custody/on-call info. Timeline: ~one week.

Karthik — can you assemble the custody details (who holds keys, HSM/KMS notes, FIPS where applicable) and produce the CSV roster. Use the internal field names: component, subprocessor, region(s), residency, key_custody (ephemeral/persistent), kms_provider, fips_level, transitive_subprocessors.

Ben — can you confirm vendor on-call contacts and incident SLA for each subprocessor, plus whether we can share phone/email or need to supply a redacted vendor contact? If suppliers require a POA/NDA before we share direct contacts, flag it.

I'll coordinate delivery and produce a short cover memo for Helix summarizing our controls.

Naomi
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for subprocessor residency + key custody mapping for EU payment flows

Naomi — attaching the CSV roster and a summary below. I focused on the EU payment path (tokenization -> inference cache -> streaming telemetry). Notes and flags first:

1) Key custody patterns
- Redwood KMS (managed HSM) — persistent signing keys for customer billing runs. HSM vendor: CloudSafe HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 evidence available). Keys are logically scoped per-customer; we do not export private key material.
- Ephemeral keys: EdgeCache and Ingest-side transformers use per-request ephemeral keys (rotated < 5 mins), no persistent storage of key material.

2) Subprocessor examples (in CSV):
- KeyVaultCo — Role: KMS/HSM provider; Region: eu-west-1; Residency: key material custodial region eu; key_custody: persistent; kms_provider: CloudSafe; fips_level: FIPS 140-2 L3; transitive_subprocessors: none listed.
- EdgeAccel Ltd — Role: inference edge caching; Region: eu-central-1, us-east-1; Residency: EU for eu flows; key_custody: ephemeral only; kms_provider: none; fips_level: n/a; transitive_subprocessors: uses CDN provider for routing.
- TelemetryStream Inc — Role: telemetry pipeline (aggregated non-PII metrics); Region: eu-west-1; Residency: EU; key_custody: no keys; transitive_subprocessors: analytics vendor (DataPulse).

3) Transitive note: some vendors rely on analytics or logging processors based in US; for EU payment flows we mark those as "out-of-scope" for payment data (we route minimal telemetry and obfuscate identifiers).

4) Evidence attached: redwood_subproc_roster_20260809.csv (roster with columns matching Helix template). I also uploaded supporting artifacts to the shared drive (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-Example).

Open questions: Ben — do we have vendor contact emails we can share verbatim, or should we supply redacted titles and route contact through Redwood? Also, Helix asked about CAIQ mapping — do we want to produce a CAIQ slice specifically for payment controls or hand them the full CAIQ?

Karthik
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subproc_roster_20260809.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 08:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for subprocessor residency + key custody mapping for EU payment flows

Thanks — quick answers and attachments.

1) On-call / escalation: we can share vendor point-of-contact names and roles; phone numbers are vendor-controlled and many request routing through an intermediary. For Helix we'll provide vendor POC names + on-call role + Redwood escalation bridge (oncall@redwood.com) as primary route.

2) SLA/MTTR: included in roster where available — typical incident response SLA for these providers is 1 hour for critical incidents; we capture contract-backed MTTR where it exists.

3) Attached: ephemeral_key_custody_matrix.pdf (explains where ephemeral keys are generated, rotation windows, and non-persistence guarantees). Also attaching SOC snapshot zip: soc2-snapshot-202605.zip (redacted).

On CAIQ: recommend producing a focused CAIQ slice for payment-relevant controls (encryption, key mgmt, access controls, logging) rather than the full CAIQ; Helix usually prefers narrow slices for scope.

Ben
Vendor Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ephemeral_key_custody_matrix.pdf; soc2-snapshot-202605.zip

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Marquez <lucia.marquez@helixbank.com>
Cc: compliance@helixbank.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Request for subprocessor residency + key custody mapping for EU payment flows

Hi Lucia — thanks for the clarity. Please find attached the CSV roster and two supporting artifacts: redwood_subproc_roster_20260809.csv (roster), ephemeral_key_custody_matrix.pdf, and a redacted SOC2 snapshot (soc2-snapshot-202605.zip). We also uploaded the materials to the shared drive for Helix review: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-Example and filed the request under HubSpot ticket HUBSPOT-123456.

Short summary:
- Persistent key custody for payment signing is performed in our managed HSM (CloudSafe) with FIPS-validated modules; regionally scoped per EU customer flows.
- Edge and inference caches only use ephemeral per-request keys; no persistent storage of key material.
- Some analytics/logging subprocessors are US-based but do not receive payment tokens or PII for EU flows — routing rules and obfuscation applied.
- For vendor on-call we provided vendor POC names + Redwood intermediary (oncall@redwood.com) as primary escalation path; phone numbers can be made available under NDA (if required).

If you'd like a CAIQ slice focusing on payment controls, we can produce that within 3 business days — confirm and we'll include it. Otherwise please let us know if Helix requires vendor phone numbers or a signed NDA prior to sharing.

Best regards,
Naomi
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subproc_roster_20260809.csv; ephemeral_key_custody_matrix.pdf; soc2-snapshot-202605.zip
